summary: All four attempt-1 mutations now killed with zero source change; 35/39 of my own mutations killed; gates green; scope held; every surviving mutant is genuinely equivalent or a non-criterion assertion gap.
acceptance_proven: yes - every clause pinned: keyboard open, no option matches 'adsad', exactly one row reading '+ Criar novo contato "adsad"', inside role=listbox, as aria-activedescendant, Enter calls onCreate and closes, Escape closes with neither callback
four_mutations_killed: yes - (1) create row relocated to be a sibling of role=listbox: KILLED, 2 tests Red ('shows the create row...', 'keeps the create row visible...'); (2) aria-activedescendant pointed at a non-existent id: KILLED on both branches, create-branch bogus id fails 2 tests, option-branch bogus id fails 4; (3) vacuous disabled test fixed properly - it now drives a keydown that really reaches the React handler, asserts defaultPrevented===false, and is backed by a new positive-control test, so deleting handleTriggerKeyDown's disabled guard goes Red; (4) trigger-toggle deviation now tested - onClick={() => openPanel()} fails 'closes an open panel when the trigger is clicked again'
equivalent_mutant_claim: upheld - I enumerated openPanel's callers myself: only handleTriggerKeyDown (which returns at its own disabled guard first) and the trigger button's onClick (element carries disabled={disabled}). No useImperativeHandle; the forwarded ref publishes only the raw HTMLButtonElement; no onFocus/onBlur; none of the three effects calls it. I proved it empirically rather than from memory: a throwaway probe attacked <Combobox disabled> with 63 distinct input paths (ref.current.click, btn.click, dispatched click on button/inner span/chevron svg, mousedown, mouseup, focus, blur, dispatched focus/focusin/blur, form.reset, dispatched submit, and keydown+keyup for Enter/Space/ArrowDown/ArrowUp/a/Escape/Tab/Home/End on both button and span). Pristine: all 63 leave the panel closed. With openPanel's guard deleted: all 63 still leave it closed. No reachable input path exists, so the mutant is behaviour-preserving - an equivalent mutant, not a coverage hole. Not held against the slice; keeping the guard as defence-in-depth is fine.
source_unchanged_from_attempt1: yes - a7fbcc5 reachable via reflog; git diff a7fbcc5..1fb35e9 touches only the test file (+55/-1, the deletion being a renamed test title). Blob hashes identical pre-amend, post-amend and in the worktree: combobox.tsx b0cfae0d, combobox-filter.ts 1239554b
new_survivors: 4 of 39, none a defect and none on a criterion clause or the a11y contract. (a) openPanel disabled guard - EQUIVALENT MUTANT, see above. (b) nativeEvent.stopImmediatePropagation() removed from the Escape branch - EQUIVALENT MUTANT: I probed with a native document keydown listener (the Radix DismissableLayer shape) and got 0 calls both pristine and with stopImmediatePropagation gone, because React's synthetic stopPropagation forwards to the native event and React 18 dispatches at the root container below document; removing the load-bearing stopPropagation DOES turn the test Red (native listener 1 call), so the behaviour is covered and only the redundant third call is unpinned. The plan slightly overclaims which of the three calls test 20 pins. (c) onCreate?.(query.trim()) -> onCreate?.(query) - REAL BUT MINOR GAP, not a defect: no test commits a create with surrounding whitespace, so the payload trim is unpinned; shipped code is correct, criterion query 'adsad' has no whitespace. Recommend asserting onCreate('Maria') for input '  Maria  ' in the adoption slice. (d) overflow-y-auto removed from the options scroll container - REAL WEAK ASSERTION, not a defect: test 10's closest('.overflow-y-auto')===null is a negative assertion with no positive control and stays green when the class is deleted outright, so it does not lock the pinned-footer design the plan says it locks; the criterion clause that matters (create row inside the listbox) is separately and strongly pinned. Recommend asserting the options container itself carries overflow-y-auto.
